Major divergence between elos: The lower your elo, the less upgrades you need to be "stable" and thus lower elo players should generally roll less than high elo players on 3-2.
After your 3-2 rolldown, you should attempt to rebuild your economy to 50g.
Once you reach 50g (it might be later than 3-5), start slow rolling down to ~52g each turn. Try to avoid rolling to exactly 50g as any unit you want to buy in shop will put you below 50g.

If you are high HP relative to the lobby, continue slow rolling to 52g each turn. If you are lower HP, you should roll to hit your first 2-cost 3 star on 4-1 or 4-2. If you have to roll below 30g, your placement is usually capped at 3rd or 4th.

If you are still high HP (70+), you can continue to slow roll. Otherwise, in the majority of cases, you should roll deep for your 3-stars here. If your HP is low, you can even go to 0 gold looking for your 3-stars. If you have your 3-stars and can afford to level to 7 with 10g+, do so.

comps.name: Ahri Zyra
tips: There are two main versions: The Shen Amumu version and the Lillia Rakan version. Shen Amumu looks better, although Lillia Rakan gets 1 more trait if you have Bronze for Life
One strength of this line is you can easily hit the full board on level 8 since it doesn't require any 5-costs and can be quite strong with combat augments

The main reasoning behind the unit to left of Sett is to prevent Kha'Zix from walking up and immediately killing your corner carry. The main objective for positioning against Kha'Zix is to make sure he can't walk into your frontline at the start of the fight.
This means you don't need the unit to the left of Sett if there are no Kha'Zix players in your pool.

comps.name: Akali Reroll
tips: While some have played this line with Yorick or Rakan instead of Ornn, Ornn seems much better and has a better level 4 and 5 board.
This is more of a 1-cost reroll line than 1 and 2 cost reroll. The goal is to 3 star all 5 1-costs to unlock the Solar trait breakpoint.
When rolling in Stage 3, try to only buy Starfall, Starting Town, an econ wisp, or item wisp (permanent items, not temporary). Field of Mice was disabled in 18.2.

Can also stop rolling for wisp on an item wisp such as the item shop or the one that gives a component after a certain number of champions die. This comp can itemize up to 5 units easily which means items are highly valuable and it isn't that expensive to hit the final board compared to other comps.

Akali can be played as AD or AP. Both are fine. AD is slightly easier to play around since you'll want to build Sunder for Camille anyway, but if you have AP items it's fine to play around AP Akali. You can see both builds by clicking "AD" or "AP" under Akali in the Builds section.

Part of what makes this line situationally better than the Kayle reroll line is the fact it can win early rounds much easier and is less expensive to stabilize on since it doesn't require any 2-cost 3 stars.

comps.name: Alune Fast 9
tips: Late-game, there are a few ways to play the endgame board. The main flex slots are Lillia, Fiddlesticks, Morgana, and Ivern. A few examples are provided of how you can flex the endgame board. Lunar, Primal, or Coven Lux should always go on the final board (Turtle Blessing).

To fit Lux, you can either drop Morgana or Ivern. Ivern is better long-term, but Morgana 2 can be hard to drop at some points in the game so you'll have to make a judgment call on what's best for your spot.
Alune is highly flexible with her items. Just make sure she has at least 1 mana item (Shojin, Blue Buff, Adaptive, Nashor with JG) and 1 AP item.
The champions on the edge positioning is useful against Kha'Zix (you want to prevent him from walking up to your frontline row), but otherwise is generally unnecessary.
AD items in the item priority matrix are if you are dropped many swords, in which case you should play the Elder Dragon variation.
It's not mandatory to play Rakan + Lillia. Can play Hecarim instead of Rakan and drop Lillia for a 5 cost (no Defender).

comps.name: Azir Reroll
tips: Kha'Zix only needs to get Executioner in this line before you start sacrificing him to the Blackthorn hex. That is part of what makes this line unique: Because it plays around Azir carry with a non-Blackthorn tank, you can sacrifice an AP unit instead of tank unit.

This means you can play this line even if you do not have early Kha'Zix copies. Most people do not reroll Kha'Zix unless they have him in Stage 2, so make sure to scout early to ensure you are uncontested.

At 3 stars, sacrificing Kha'Zix provides Azir over 40% damage amp and 6 mana per second so focus on giving Azir Gunblade, AP items, and Attack Speed. Striker's is an acceptable damage amp item because it gives crit.

Sacrificing Kha'Zix also means you don't technically need Rageblade. It's still a good item when paired with Rabadon's or Archangel, but because Azir has an additional 6 mana per second he will still cast often and his cast gives him 150% Attack Speed.
This means ideally every Azir build has Gunblade + Rabadon's or Archangel, but the 3rd item is relatively flexible.

Void Staff is ideal because it is a great Azir item before you can get 3 full proper items on him. If you have to build Ionic Spark instead, try to get into a place where it goes onto Sett instead of Vi (always aim to have 3 "real" tank items on Vi). It's better to play Void on Azir than Spark on Vi
Since Zyra is the best holder of utility and secondary carry items, it's possible that it's better to play Zyra over Sett on level 7. Be flexible based on your items and frontline needs.

comps.name: Blossom
tips: The main board is 5 Blossom + Juggernaut + Brawler + 2 Flex Slots. Vi + Sivir + Zyra is common, but can also play Maokai over Vi and Zyra can be replaced with Ivern or Lux. Sivir is not as important if not playing around Vi.
This comp is flexible on Emblems thanks to the flexible unit slots.
Blossom Emblem is strong because it allows you to play 7 Blossom on 8 consistently even without Ahri. The extra gold from 7 Blossom helps you hit the full board and go 9.

5 Blossom boards tend to cap higher than 7 Blossom boards since the primary benefit of 7 Blossom is the extra gold. Play 7 Blossom as long as possible, then look to move out of 7 Blossom late game once you need to stabilize.
Position Ahri on the same side as the opponent's carry. Much of the strength of this comp comes from the fact that Ahri can kill the opponent's backline before their tank.

Ahri's ability to kill the backline is part of why having perfect items on her and 2 starring her as soon as possible are important. It helps give her enough damage to ensure she can kill the backline rather than leave them barely alive.

Part of why Executioner Emblem is so good for this line is because it helps Ahri meet the threshold killing backline by giving her an execute AND it enables playing Kennen which also helps kill the backline.

comps.name: Blossom Fast 9
tips: The main concept behind this Fast 9 line is to play around Ahri + Sett + Ashe. This leads to almost always playing around Alune and Gnar. From there you need to fill out the frontline.

There are four Jug options: Vi + Sivir, Amumu + Kennen, Rakan, and Maokai. Rakan makes it possible to crossover with a Vanguard such as Taric, Sentinel, or Diana. Maokai is good if found early enough as he's the best tank in the game if he farms enough HP from his trait.
In general the goal for the frontline is to play around upgraded units, not the perfect optimal board. Flex the appropriate packages based on what frontline units you hit.

tips: The nerfs to Dark Ritual in Patch 18.4 have made this comp weaker than it was before. The comp is more conditional now - aim to play if you have good components / can play good losses or need direction.
Prioritize taking Cassiopeia on first carousel regardless of the component most of the time - It's more important to make sure you get 4 Coven as early as possible than perfect items.

Two ways to play this comp: Reroll or Fast 8. Reroll version of comp should roll on level 6 and 7 and go for Elise 3 + ideally Cassio 3. For Fast 8, hold extra copies of Cassio on Level 8 and try to 3 star her while playing 6 Vanguard or 4 Vanguard + Legendaries.

Do not pass by Coven Lux if you hit her. She is a massive spike - her passive and ability help all your Coven units, plus she does a ton of damage with the AP from augment.

tips: Archangel is better than Rabadon's. As part of the Unreal Engine transition, damage over time (DoT) champions now have their DoTs update their damage as the caster's AP increases rather than snapshotting on cast.

The idea behind the Fiddle build is to have him cast as much as possible to help Cassiopeia take enemies down and heal himself. Adaptive Helm increases his mana gain from Flora Fatalis and he gets plenty of tankiness from 6 Defender and Gunblade. Titan's gives him CC immunity.

comps.name: Pebbles Reroll
tips: This is a comp that was played during PBE, but no longer played as Riftbeasts vertical is generally just better. Can consider playing from Worth the Wait Pebbles, otherwise play other lines. This is primary reason for D-tier ranking.
While you can play around 5 Riftbeast for the shops before hitting Pebbles 3, the best endgame board appears to be 5 Invoker which helps Pebbles go infinite.
This comp can use many tears, so always almost always prioritize them on Carousel.

Pebbles needs ~17.1 Mana Regen (round up to 18) + Alpha Mark to go infinite. Going infinite does not look mandatory, but it is worth noting. Double mana allows for Sentinel Alpha Mark and can still go infinite (need 2 Sentinel casts with 21 regen+).
If you build double mana on Pebbles (Blue + Blue or Blue + Adaptive), the last item really wants to be Rabadon's or Pebbles will not do enough damage.

Alpha Mark is not solved for this line. Current theory I have is this: Below 17 mana regen use it on Sentinel or Scuttle. Between 17 and 20 use on Pebbles for infinite cast. From 21 to 23, use on Sentinel for infinite cast + teamwide regen. It's possible Scuttle is always better.
All the mana values mentioned here are for 70 Max Mana and 35% Mana Drain per second, so verify against Pebble's tooltip in case these tips go out of date.

tips: Must have 5 Riftbeast by 3-1. Roll for it if need be (sometimes correct to roll for it in Stage 2). Ideally want to minimize rolls before level 7. This is why having at least 3 copies of Cinderling or Pebbles early is important so you can reasonably hit 3-star without rolling much before 7.

The comp can be played as fast 9 in rare circumstances where you streak with nearly a natural Cinderling or Pebbles 3, but this is quite rare so the reroll variant is far more popular.

tips: This comp was practically unplayable before Patch 18.5, but now is viable after buffs to both Tristana and 4 Fae. The comp is much better with Fae Emblem still as it allows you to drop Xayah for Rengar which is a major spike.

tips: General Kha'Zix upgrade order is Ravager > Executioner or Spellweaver > Rapidfire. Executioner is better than Spellweaver if you have an Executioner.
Avoid playing from spots where you can't itemize either Rengar or Kha'Zix early as the early takedowns help this comp stay on tempo.

Generally it is better to itemize Rengar before Kha'Zix as he farms gold which helps hit the board.
